Brand guidelines · version 0.3 · October 2026
Contents

Less is more. When in doubt, remove.

01 · Positioning

Anti-brand.
Incidentally cool.

NORA looks like it isn't trying to sell anything. The logo is an authentication mark, found inside the temple by the person who owns the pair. Restraint is the brand.

  • Made inSabae, Fukui, Japan. 100%. No offshore or hybrid production.
  • Edition333 per colorway per style. Hand-engraved and numbered, X/333.
  • Price$1,111. One price.
  • StylesBlake, Sunny, Bella.
  • LensesNylon (polyamide).
  • SoldDirect only, at ohitsnora.com. No wholesale.
  • ForEveryone. Unisex from launch.
  • CompanyOhitsnora Corporation (Texas), doing business as NORA Eyewear.
02 · Voice

Near-silent. Facts, not adjectives.

Write like this

Sabae, Japan. 333 pieces. N° 001/333.
Black frame. Black lens.
One price. $1,111.
The waitlist is open.
Hand-engraved inside the temple.

Never like this

Elevate your look with our iconic shades!
We're obsessed with craftsmanship.
Only a few left. Don't miss out!
The ultimate statement piece.
For the modern gentleman.

Short. No exclamation points. No first-person hype. No gendered copy. No invented press, quotes, stockists or numbers.

03 · Banned words

Never in NORA copy.

luxury
exclusive
elevate
premium
curated
iconic
timeless
must-have
game-changer

If a sentence needs one of these words, delete the sentence. The original lockup's "LUXURY EYEWEAR" is kept on file only.

04 · Less is more

Remove until it breaks. Then add one thing back.

Do · one markThe case: a blind deboss of the monogram. Nothing else.
Don't · pattern the logo
Monogram prints, all-over logos, logo hardware.
Do · one line
Sabae, Japan.
One fact per layout.
Don't · explain
Handcrafted with passion by master artisans using only the finest materials, each pair is a testament to our uncompromising commitment to quality and style.
Adjectives, claims, paragraphs.
04 · Less is more

One accent. One line. One mark.

Do · one violet moment
N° —/333
Violet is a spark, never a surface.
Don't · violet text or violet grounds
Body copy in violet on black is hard to read. At 3.4:1 it fails the contrast test for text.
Never as body text, never as a background.
Do · blank exterior The outside of the frame carries nothing.
Don't · more than one line
Boxes, double rules, dividers everywhere.

Positioning map

NORA takes the quiet, cult corner.

Loud means the logo or hardware does the talking. Cult means scarcity, numbering and a following the brand does not chase.

JMM is the nearest neighbor, but its collaborations and storytelling pull it toward the center. Maison Margiela is quiet but sells broadly. Nobody else sits where NORA plans to: no exterior mark, a fixed number and one price.

Positions are NORA's judgment, not measured data.

      NORA · D2 Logo system08
      Vectorization check

      Trace laid over the source.

      Source at 1.7× with the vector outline in violet

      Difference map · bright = mismatch

      PartAvg. differenceInk area

      The monogram and wordmark match the source within about 1% of ink area. The only visible differences are edge softness from the source's JPEG compression. The descriptor reads heavier because the source letters are soft gray and the vector is solid ink. The source is about 220 px wide, so fine detail below one source pixel cannot be verified.

      A designer's master file should replace this trace when one exists, especially for the trademark filing.

      NORA · D5 Typography03
      Pairing

      Do less.

      Do
      Blake · Black / Black
      N° 001/333
      Sabae, Japan · $1,111
      Don't
      Only 333 made!
      Get yours before it's gone
      Do

      Made in Sabae, Japan. Hand-engraved inside the temple. Numbered one to 333.

      Body: Cormorant 400. One label in Jost.
      Don't

      Body copy set in tracked capitals is hard to read past one line, and four weights on one page is three too many.

      Rules: two faces, three weights at most per layout. Jost stays small. No bold. No exclamation points. Never retype the wordmark in either face.

      NORA · D5 Typography05
      D6 · Imagery and graphic style

      Caught, never sold.

      Two treatments. Black-and-white for the object, almost always. Low-key color for people, rarely. Darkness dominates both.

      NORA · D6 Imagery01
      Sample: crop of NORA's amber macro, converted
      Primary · black and white

      The product as an object.

      • High contrast. True blacks. Let shadows fill in.
      • One light. Hard or soft, never a lit-from-everywhere studio.
      • Negative space. The frame takes up no more than a third of the image.
      • Surface stays real. No retouching of acetate grain, metal or engraving.
      • Converted in post. Shoot color RAW, convert to black and white. Keep a color master.
      • Macro is welcome in either treatment: acetate, metal, engraving, leather.
      NORA · D6 Imagery02
      Diagram: one warm practical source, the rest falls to black
      Secondary · low-key color · sparingly

      People, in the dark.

      • One practical light in the scene: a lamp, a bar light, a window. Warm.
      • Darkness dominates. Most of the image falls to black.
      • Candid. Faces turned away, in profile or in silhouette. Nobody looks at the lens.
      • Nothing staged. If it looks lit for a shoot, reshoot.
      • Unisex. Cast and pose without gender cues. The same direction for everyone.
      • At most one in three campaign images uses color.

      Reference: refs/mood/mood-01 (direction only, never published; not supplied yet)

      NORA · D6 Imagery03
      Never

      If it sells, it's wrong.

      Smiling at the cameraStock warmth. Anyone looking into the lens.
      Studio-white e-commerceFloating packshots on white, gloss and reflections.
      Beaches, yachts, champagneLifestyle props that tell you what to feel.
      Gendered posesHand-on-hip, chin-down glamour, power stances.
      Other brandsNo visible logos, posters or labels in frame. Check backgrounds.
      Fake 3D and rendersNo photoreal CGI of the product. Real or line drawing only.

      NORA · D6 Imagery05
      Macro detail list

      Material, up close.

      • The hand engraving inside the temple: the stroke, not just the number
      • Sunny's acetate layers and pattern at the temple tip, backlit
      • Blake's black acetate polish: one specular line
      • Bella's metal surface and joints OPEN: confirm metal type before naming it
      • Hinges and screws
      • The lens edge and gradient transition
      • Case leather grain, the fold and the magnetic flap
      • The card's paper and print
      • Sabae workshop hands and tools, if access is given OPEN: ask Sabaeframe
      For the photographer

      Technical brief.

      • Shoot RAW, color. Black-and-white conversion in post.
      • Deliver at 4:5 (feed), 9:16 (stories) and 3:2 (web), cropped from one master
      • Leave room: the hairline and labels need the lower third of a 4:5 frame clear
      • No visible logos, signs or posters from other brands anywhere in frame
      • Clean dust, keep texture. No skin smoothing, no material retouching.
      • File names: style_shot_treatment, e.g. blake_05_bw.tif
      NORA · D6 Imagery06
      Graphic devices · approved

      Three devices. One per layout.

      The Prism

      The case profile as a hairline triangle. A marker for sections, highlights and the box seal. Never filled, never holds the logo.

      OPEN: proportions from case sketches

      —/333

      The Numeral

      N° —/333 before launch. Real numbers only on the card and the frame. "N° 001/333" only as a labeled sample.

      The Hairline

      The lockup rule as the one line in a layout, at 61.8% of the height. Headlines rest on it; labels hang below.

      Leopard is not a device. It is a material accent: at most about 5% of a layout, and only from NORA's own acetate once photographed.
